$comment: What this mod believes about vanilla, recorded so a game patch that moves any of it fails a
test instead of changing how the game plays. Checked by tests/run_baseline.sh; regenerated
'overrides' is derived: every method an adapter overrides that vanilla declares, with the
default argument values vanilla gives it. GDScript takes defaults from the most-derived
method, so a default that moves in vanilla and not here is a silent behaviour change that
'bodies' is the hand-kept half, and the one worth reading. Each entry is a vanilla method
whose logic this mod copies rather than calls. Nothing catches those drifting apart -- the
copy still compiles, it is just no longer what vanilla does -- so the method's source is
hashed and a change makes the test say which copy has to be re-read, and why.
'signals' are the ones the mod looks up by name at runtime. A renamed signal is not a parse
error; it is a feature that silently stops happening.

bodies.why: The override is this body with the RunData.can_combine() line dropped, because that call is typed WeaponData and cannot be asked about an item. Everything else about which buttons show is copied.
The override widens vanilla's answer and then repeats the co-op half of this condition by hand: 'not RunData.is_coop_run or focused'.
tweaks_recycle_item() is this method line for line against the items half of the gear container, with is_weapon false and add_recycled() deliberately left out.
The adapter repeats the two lines this method runs for a positive gain_pct_gold_start_wave, for the waves past nb_of_waves where this one skips them.
The endless harvesting decay is one line in here. remove_stat() is skipped on the strength of this being the only place the harvesting stat is removed.
The adapter re-runs the tail of this method that vanilla skips for a weapon or an unearned challenge -- the same text, the same show, the same activate().
The adapter rewrites the ban label this method builds, because vanilla builds both halves of it out of RunData.BAN_MAX_TOKEN.
The adapter recognises the tick vanilla spawned on by cur_spawn_delay == 0, which is this method's own state machine and nothing the engine guarantees.
spawn() pops exactly one entity per call. VANILLA_PER_TICK and the whole 40-a-second model in core/spawn_rate.gd are read off this method and _physics_process() together.
The adapter makes the retry half of this screen visible and writes the retry line, which this method writes only when vanilla's own option is on.

signals.why: Connected by name for cursed enemies, and walked with get_signal_connection_list() to find the DLC's own curse behaviour. A rename is not a parse error -- it is All Cursed silently doing nothing to enemies.

Walked with get_signal_connection_list() to reach the shop that built the popup, because the vanilla handler is typed WeaponData and cannot be overridden for an item. A rename is a Recycle button that does nothing.
